clauses.normalized_text: Unlike TLS over TCP, QUIC applications which want to send data do not send it through TLS “application_data” records.
clauses.raw_text: Unlike TLS over TCP, QUIC applications which want to send data do not send it through TLS “application_data” records.

clauses.normalized_text: Rather, they send it as QUIC STREAM frames which are then carried in QUIC packets.
clauses.raw_text: Rather, they send it as QUIC STREAM frames which are then carried in QUIC packets.

clauses.normalized_text: QUIC carries TLS handshake data in CRYPTO frames, each of which consists of a contiguous block of handshake data identified by an offset and length.
clauses.raw_text: QUIC carries TLS handshake data in CRYPTO frames, each of which consists of a contiguous block of handshake data identified by an offset and length.

clauses.normalized_text: Those frames are packaged into QUIC packets and encrypted under the current TLS encryption level.
clauses.raw_text: Those frames are packaged into QUIC packets and encrypted under the current TLS encryption level.

clauses.normalized_text: As with TLS over TCP, once TLS handshake data has been delivered to QUIC, it is QUIC’s responsibility to deliver it reliably.
clauses.raw_text: As with TLS over TCP, once TLS handshake data has been delivered to QUIC, it is QUIC’s responsibility to deliver it reliably.

clauses.raw_text: If QUIC needs to retransmit that data, it MUST use the same keys even if TLS has already updated to newer keys.

clauses.raw_text: Each encryption level is associated with a different flow of bytes, which is reliably transmitted to the peer in CRYPTO frames.

clauses.raw_text: When TLS provides handshake octets to be sent, they are appended to the current flow and any packet that includes the CRYPTO frame is protected using keys from the corresponding encryption level.

clauses.raw_text: QUIC takes the unprotected content of TLS handshake records as the content of CRYPTO frames.

clauses.normalized_text: TLS record protection is not used by QUIC.
clauses.raw_text: TLS record protection is not used by QUIC.

clauses.raw_text: QUIC assembles CRYPTO frames into QUIC packets, which are protected using QUIC packet protection.

clauses.raw_text: When an endpoint receives a QUIC packet containing a CRYPTO frame from the network, it proceeds as follows:

clauses.normalized_text: If the packet was in the TLS receiving encryption level, sequence the data into the input flow as usual.
clauses.raw_text: If the packet was in the TLS receiving encryption level, sequence the data into the input flow as usual.

clauses.normalized_text: If the result of this process is that new data is available, then it is delivered to TLS in order.

clauses.raw_text: If the packet is from a previously installed encryption level, it MUST not contain data which extends past the end of previously received data in that flow.
